# Pinned JuiceFS SDK library source

This nested module is JuiceFS v1.3.1's complete `pkg/` library tree, its `cmd/` CLI tree and root `main.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, and Apache-2.0 `LICENSE`, copied byte-for-byte from the module archive verified by the existing root `go.sum` (upstream tag v1.3.1, commit e0032b2ae5e9603403ca955eed7d05426f6f2f8c). It omits documentation, integration tests and SDK examples. The library replaces the SDK for this application; the CLI is built into the one JuiceFS executable the app ships. Existing copyright headers are retained.

The root module has a version-specific, repository-relative `replace` directive. Ordinary `go build` and `go test` use this source without environment flags, overlays, network forks, or edits to the shared module cache. Existing root dependency replacements remain in force.

The first upstream source change is `patches/0001-synchronize-upload-failure.patch`: `wSlice` uses an atomic cancellation flag instead of an unsynchronized error interface. The upload loop only needed a failed/not-failed signal; `Finish` still returns the original error. This fixes the read/write race exposed when one upload fails while sibling uploads continue. It does not join those workers, change retry limits, establish durability, or permit releasing process ownership early.

`SOURCE.json` records archive provenance, the verified module checksum, every upstream and local source hash, and the patch hash. From the repository root run `python3 scripts/verify-juicefs-sdk.py`; add `--archive /path/to/v1.3.1.zip` to independently verify the source against the complete upstream module ZIP. The root SDK acceptance test's corrupt-provider case exercises actual upload/Fsync failure under the race detector; keep that oracle when changing this patch.

`patches/0002-create-only-object-writes.patch` adds the optional `SupportCreateOnly` interface. S3 and MinIO send `If-None-Match: *`; HTTP 412 returns `os.ErrExist`, while conflicts and uncertain replies remain failures. Sharded storage forwards through its existing raw-key routing. File storage syncs the parent directory chain and a private file before publishing with a no-replace hard link, then syncs its parent; uncertain linked targets are retained. Configured directories must be trusted and stable. Existing ordinary `Put` behavior is unchanged. This adds four reviewed object-library source changes; it does not establish an operation manifest, exclude external writers/deletions, or qualify provider power-loss behavior.

`patches/0003-inode-bound-slice-allocation.patch` adds the optional `meta.InodeSliceAllocator` hook to the existing shared VFS writer. Allocation is serialized per slice before invoking a recording allocator; nonretryable registration errors do not expose an ID or retry forever. Metadata implementations without the interface retain ordinary `NewSlice` behavior. A controlled overlapping initial/Fsync test covers success and refusal. This hook does not stop background workers or grant publication/durability authority.

`patches/0004-preflight-link-counters.patch` validates each hard-link parent counter under WATCH before queuing namespace effects. Wrong-type, noncanonical, negative and overflowing counters are refused; same-parent increments are checked together, and the inode link count cannot wrap. A concurrent counter mutation aborts EXEC and is checked again. Actual Redis/SDK tests cover retained bytes, collisions, ordinary links and a held-EXEC mutation. This prevents the diagnosed counter failures from partially publishing a link; it does not provide rollback for other Redis runtime errors, resolve ambiguous EXEC replies, or authorize media receipts or local spool retirement.


The fourth patch also supplies optional `PublishNewName` and `RecoverNewName`
Redis methods. Publication guards a captured root-to-parent chain and exact
private stage identity, rejects an occupied target and configured quotas, and
updates public-link directory accounting in the same EXEC as namespace effects.
Recovery recognizes exact private/public tuples and repairs public parent totals
with a watched absolute write. Callers must fence previous processes and retain
immutable publication intent before using these methods. Ordinary Link behavior
is unchanged. This does not issue a durability receipt or retire local custody.

## Bundled executable and patch 0005

The app ships its own JuiceFS at `Contents/MacOS/juicefs`; the `jm5` CLI build places it beside `build/jm5`. `scripts/build-bundled-juicefs.sh` (used by `build-app.sh` and `build-cli.sh`) first runs `scripts/verify-juicefs-sdk.py`, then builds this module (`go build .` here, so upstream's own `go.mod`/`go.sum` choose the dependencies) with the tags and ldflags in `SOURCE.json` `binary`, and refuses a binary whose `--version` differs from `binary.version_output`. The runtime (`internal/juicefsbin`) resolves only that sibling executable and refuses any other configured path; it never searches PATH or Homebrew. `scripts/verify-build.sh` checks that the bundled juicefs exists, has the app's signer and reports the pinned version, and onboarding preflight checks the same.

`patches/0005-owner-keeps-kernel-mount.patch` makes the kernel mount belong to the process that started JuiceFS. Upstream v1.3.1 answers SIGTERM/SIGINT with `doUmount(mp, true)`, which on macOS runs `umount -f <path>`; the unmount stops new FUSE requests, then upstream flushes and closes the session. A path can name a newer, different mount by the time a signal is handled, so the patch keeps that ordering without the unmount:

- `installHandler` (`cmd/mount_unix.go`) hands SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to `pkg/jmsignal`, which (1) stops the FUSE server with go-fuse `Server.Shutdown`, (2) runs `FlushAll`, (3) closes the session, releases object storage and exits 0 (1 if the flush failed). Requests that reach the kernel after step 1 wait there and are never acknowledged by this process; they fail when it exits. Stop is attempted once (patch 0008 changed this): go-fuse's own 10 s limit already bounds it, and if it fails (server not serving yet, or a request busy past 10 s, after which go-fuse resumes) the process flushes and closes its session anyway while the server still serves.
- The whole sequence has upstream's 30 s deadline. On expiry the process exits 2 without closing the session; Redis treats it like a crash and stale-session cleanup reclaims it later. Buffered data that did not reach object storage is lost from JuiceFS. JuiceMount runs without `--writeback` unless `JM_FUSE_WRITEBACK=1`, so nothing is staged locally; the spool keeps its safety copy because the drainer's close never returned. With `--writeback`, blocks already staged in `<cache-dir>/rawstaging` survive and the next mount uploads them, but a slice whose metadata commit did not happen is still not part of any file. Repeated signals during the sequence are logged and ignored, so a supervisor retrying SIGTERM cannot skip the flush; SIGKILL remains the owner's escalation. Neither exit code is `meta.UmountCode`.
- `doUmount` (`cmd/umount.go`) always returns a refusal, so the supervisor-restart, broken-mountpoint and `juicefs umount` paths cannot unmount either. JuiceMount runs JuiceFS in direct service mode (`JFS_SUPERVISOR` set, no `-d`), where none of those paths run.
- `pkg/fuse` no longer calls `fssrv.Unmount()` (a path `unmount(2)` on macOS) when `Serve` returns.

In the pinned `github.com/juicedata/go-fuse/v2` fork, `Server.Shutdown` does not unmount. It sets a shutdown flag so readers stop reading `/dev/macfuse`, wakes readers blocked in `read(2)` by running `df <mountpoint>` (a `statfs` read of the path; on a path that now names another mount it only fails to wake ours, and Shutdown then gives up), interrupts in-flight requests after 3 s, gives up after 10 s, and keeps the FUSE fd. While readers are blocked it starts a `df` about every 10 ms. The fork's only path unmount is `Server.Unmount` (`syscall.Unmount(dir, 0)` on darwin), which the patched binary never calls.

`pkg/jmsignal/jmsignal.go` is JuiceMount-owned source with no upstream counterpart; `SOURCE.json` records it under `local_files`.

## Patch 0006

`patches/0006-redact-redis-url-errors-default-ipv6-port.patch` records the SDK change made by commit a9f070c ("Preserve Redis connection settings across app clients"), which had edited the source without updating `SOURCE.json`. Redis metadata and Redis object-store URL parse errors no longer echo the URL (it can carry a password). In the metadata URL only (`pkg/meta/redis.go`), a bracketed IPv6 host without a port gets 6379 instead of go-redis treating the brackets as part of the host name; the object-store URL keeps upstream port handling. It stacks on patch 0004 for `pkg/meta/redis.go`. Patches apply in name order; `scripts/verify-juicefs-sdk.py --archive` applies them to the upstream ZIP and requires the result to equal this tree.

## Patch 0007

`patches/0007-jmdeny-erofs.patch` makes a write refused by JuiceMount's per-project Redis proxy (H-8 option B) reach the caller as `EROFS` ("Read-only file system") instead of `EIO`. The proxy answers a refused command or transaction with `-JMDENY <REASON> proj=<ino> holder=<principal>@<host> epoch=<n>`, after sending `DISCARD` upstream for a held `EXEC`, so nothing in that transaction committed. `errno` (`pkg/meta/utils.go`) maps an error starting with `JMDENY` to `EROFS` without the stack-trace log. `shouldRetry` (`pkg/meta/redis.go`) does not list the token, so the transaction is attempted once. In `pkg/vfs/writer.go`, a slice whose commit returns `EROFS` joins `ENOENT`/`ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT`: the error reaches `Flush`/`close` unchanged and the writer deletes the slice's uploaded blocks (`store.Remove`), because no metadata references that slice ID. In `pkg/meta/base.go` `compactChunk`, a compaction whose commit did not happen (`EINVAL`, which is how the Redis engine reports a refused compaction after its double-check, or `EROFS`) deletes its uploaded slice object directly with the `DeleteSlice` message when `--max-deletes 0` (the Mac mount; with deletes enabled `deleteSlice` removes it); upstream's `deleteSlice` does nothing at `--max-deletes 0`, so every refused compaction of a fragmented file in another Mac's project would leak up to 64 MiB. All three rely on the proxy invariant that JMDENY never follows a committed EXEC (documented at `errno`). juicefs has no hook to skip compaction for a project this Mac does not hold; compaction is triggered by reads (`baseMeta.Read`) and writes (`baseMeta.Write`) inside the meta engine. It stacks on patch 0003 for `writer.go`. Gates: `internal/bundledjuicefs` `TestH8BJMDENYIsEROFSSingleAttempt`, `TestH8BSliceCommitDenyCloseIsEROFS`, `TestH8BCompactionDenyLeavesNoUploadedSlice` and `TestH8BAuthRequiredMountFailsCleanly` (build tag `h8b_acceptance`, disposable Redis).

## Patch 0008

`patches/0008-stop-signal-never-remounts.patch` stops upstream's `launchMount` supervisor (`cmd/mount_unix.go`, used when `JFS_SUPERVISOR` is unset) from remounting a volume its owner stopped. The supervisor treated every child exit other than `meta.UmountCode` as a crash and restarted the mount 1 s later, so a SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP whose child exited 1 (flush failed) or 2 (`jmsignal` deadline) brought the volume back. The supervisor's signal goroutine now records that it forwarded a stop signal, and after `cmd.Wait` it returns the child's exit instead of restarting. `pkg/jmsignal` (local source) attempts Stop once; retrying a Stop that go-fuse already bounds at 10 s consumed the whole 30 s deadline before any flush. JuiceMount itself runs the service stage directly (`JFS_SUPERVISOR` set), so this supervisor path matters for a manual or CLI mount of the bundled binary.

## Gates

`internal/bundledjuicefs` gates patch 0005 from the root module: real-signal and fake-server ordering tests (no write acknowledged after the stop step), the deadline and repeated-signal test, an exact check of the effects `installHandler` wires, a source check of `doUmount`, a run of the SDK verifier, and a scan of every darwin/arm64 file in the binary's build for path unmounts (`Unmount`/`Umount` references including method values, exec of umount/diskutil/fusermount, `diskutil` strings).

`patches/0010-replacement-guards-and-cache-ownership.patch` records the guarded replacement checks in Redis and the resident-cache upload ownership changes. It stacks on the existing Redis and cached-store patches and adds the disk-cache delta. The replacement record, slice-graph helpers, Redis replacement helpers, and upload ownership tests are JuiceMount-owned files recorded under `local_files`. The archive verifier reconstructs the patched upstream files exactly; `build-app.sh` also checks the inventory before compilation.

`patches/0011-stage-birth-create-watch.patch` adds pre-MULTI WATCH coverage and fresh-create checks for exact reserved replacement stage names. It refuses unsupported ACL inheritance and prevents nonexclusive creation from adopting an existing stage. The local Redis birth helper grants no authority; atomic receipt issuance remains a disabled-by-default proxy capability until guarded upload recovery is qualified.

`patches/0012-born-stage-upload-watch.patch` prepares guarded writes and timestamp updates for born stages. It WATCHes reciprocal custody, publication, namespace and current authority keys before mutation, rejects prepared stages and preserves mode and identity. Committed files resume ordinary lease-governed operations. Prefixed Redis Cluster volumes skip this unprefixed protocol, which does not support birth creation there.

`patches/0013-security-dependencies-and-etcd-transport.patch` updates this nested module to Go 1.26.9 and the reviewed security fixes for its dependencies. Both etcd backends use the modern client TLS helper, with the configured CA mapped to `TrustedCAFile`; client registration and verification settings remain unchanged. The two local TLS test files check trusted roots, hostname rejection, mutual TLS and invalid configuration. CI scans this module with the bundled CLI tags separately from the root module, which has its own dependency graph. Root `go.sum` retains the upstream archive checksum for source provenance even though the module is replaced locally.

`patches/0014-literal-fatal-error.patch` passes an already formatted metadata configuration error to `Fatal`, preserving fatal exit behavior while treating the message as literal text. This resolves the newer Go checker's rejection of a nonconstant, zero-argument `Fatalf` call; the checker remains enabled.

`patches/0015-klauspost-compress-security-update.patch` updates `github.com/klauspost/compress` from v1.17.11 to v1.20.2 in this module's `go.mod` and `go.sum` for GO-2026-6865 (GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8), a panic on two-block frames in the `fse` and `huff0` packages that `zstd` uses; the bundled CLI reaches the affected symbols. No other dependency changes. The root module takes the same version.

`patches/0016-file-backend-beneath-root.patch` confines the `file://` object backend to its root folder on Linux.
- **How.** Every filesystem operation of the backend goes through a `fileOps` value (`pkg/object/file_ops.go`).
  - On Linux, `beneathOps` (`pkg/object/file_beneath_linux.go`) opens the root once. It then resolves every path relative to that folder with `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS)`, or with an `*at` call on a parent folder opened that way: open, create, mkdir, stat, lstat, readdir, rename, link, unlink, chmod, chown, chtimes, symlink and readlink.
  - The kernel refuses, atomically per call, any resolution that would leave the root. That covers an absolute symlink, a `..` above the root, a chain of symlinks, and a symlink swapped in between calls.
- **Links.** A symlink is still stored and read as a link (`--links`). Following one is allowed only when the kernel can prove the result stays beneath the root, so relative links inside the root work. Absolute links and links that climb above the root are not followed, even when their host path points back inside.
  - When listing with links followed (a sync without `--links`), such a link is skipped like a dangling link: it is not followed, not copied, and does not fail the sync. Each skip is logged as `skipped symlink "<path>" that leads outside the file storage root`. The `jfs://` backend (`cmd/object.go`) likewise skips, with `skipped symlink "<path>" that cannot be followed in the volume`, a link that can never be followed there: its target does not exist (ENOENT, ENOTDIR), or it is absolute or a URL, which this backend never follows (`pkg/fs` returns ENOTSUP; confirmed by reading the link). This covers macOS links such as `/Volumes/...`. Any other error (EIO, ELOOP, an unconfirmed ENOTSUP, ...) keeps upstream's handling, so it surfaces and fails the sync. The JuiceMount Manager counts these lines for the job.
  - A refusal is an `os.PathError` that wraps `EXDEV`, with the text "path resolves outside the file storage root".
- **Old kernels.** Without `openat2` (Linux before 5.6, or a seccomp policy that refuses it) every operation fails closed with a message naming the requirement.
- **Root.** The root is the folder the URI names, also without a trailing slash. Upstream treats a slash-less root as a name prefix in its parent folder; confining to that parent would widen the root, so a slash-less root can address keys beneath it but not its parent or a same-prefix sibling. Every in-tree caller (format, load, metadata backup) passes a root ending in `/`.
- **Root path.** A root given by path is opened by path: the caller must trust it. The JuiceMount Manager therefore opens each sync root itself, beneath its configured anchor with `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH)`, and passes it as `file:///proc/self/fd/N/` (the root fd is the inherited folder). A missing root given by path is created on the first write.
- **Open roots only.** With `JM_FILE_ROOT_FD_ONLY=1`, `juicefs sync` refuses a `file://` root that is not an open folder (`/proc/self/fd/N/`), so a root named by path fails loudly instead of being resolved by path (`cmd/sync.go`, `createSyncStorage`). It applies to the sync's own roots only, not to a volume's object storage. The Manager sets it whenever it passes open roots.
- **Retries.** EAGAIN or EINTR from `openat2` (a rename racing a lookup) is retried at most 64 times, then the call fails.
- **Other platforms.** Non-Linux builds keep the upstream path-based behaviour (`pathOps`, `file_beneath_other.go`). The macOS app bundles juicefs for mounting and does not run sync.
- **Gates.** `pkg/object/file_beneath_linux_test.go`, and the real-binary sync tests in `internal/manager/juicefs_beneath_test.go`, which CI runs with this module's build.
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm2`.

`patches/0017-project-fence.patch` keeps a sync's writes into the volume inside their project folders. JuiceMount leases projects (the folders a fixed number of levels below the volume root), and a sync holds only the leases of the projects it writes.
- **Switch.** `JM_SYNC_PROJECT_DEPTH=<n>` names the project level for the sync's destination: the number of key components below the destination root that name a project folder, zero or less when the root is a project folder or inside one. Without it nothing changes. A destination backend that cannot apply it fails the sync (`cmd/jm_fence.go`, `jmProjectFence`). The JuiceMount Manager sets it for every sync into the volume.
- **`file://` destination.** With a level of 1 or more, `beneathOps` (`pkg/object/file_beneath_linux.go`) resolves the project part of every path from the root with `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS`, and the rest beneath the project folder it opened. A symlink that leads into another project, a `..` above the project folder, and a symlink at or above the project level are refused, atomically per call, with an `EXDEV` error that says "outside its project folder". Symlinks that stay inside the project are followed as before.
- **`jfs://` destination.** Before each write (put, delete, symlink, chmod, chown, chtimes), `jmCheck` (`cmd/jm_fence.go`) resolves the volume path through the volume's symlinks and refuses the write by the same rules. The walk mirrors `pkg/fs` `doResolve`, which the write uses: a link's target is joined to the link's folder by name, cleaned lexically, and must name a path inside the project before it is followed. A destination prefix named through a same-project link is resolved once and then used by its real path; one that leads out of its project fails the sync. This walk is not atomic with the write. In JuiceMount's standalone mode every write also passes the Redis proxy, which checks the lease of the project the write lands in; but the proxy grants a free project to the first writer, so it is no backstop for a project nobody holds.
- **Copied links.** With `--links`, `copyLink` (`pkg/sync/sync.go`, `pkg/sync/jm_fence.go`) does not store a relative link whose target, read from where the link would be stored, leaves that project, or a link stored above the project level. It is skipped, not failed, and logged as `skipped symlink "<source path>" that leads outside its project`. The JuiceMount Manager counts these lines with the other skipped links. A `..` after a name in the target is refused too: that name may itself be a link (`y -> .`), so the check could not know where the `..` climbs from. Absolute targets are stored as before: neither confined backend follows them. A new link's parent folder must be reached through real folders only, so its place is the one its key names.
- **Gates.** `pkg/object/jm_fence_linux_test.go`, `pkg/sync/jm_fence_test.go`, and the real-binary tests in `internal/manager/lease_links_test.go`.
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm3`. The Manager requires `-jm3` for confined roots and `--links`, and refuses any sync into the volume with an older or stock juicefs.

`patches/0018-ranged-first-read.patch` lets a small cold read at the start of a block return before the whole block arrives.
- **Before.** Upstream reads a byte range from the object store only when the read starts inside a block (`boff > 0`). A cold read at offset 0 downloaded the whole block (4 MiB by default) before it returned, so the time to the first byte was the time of one full block download.
- **Now.** A read of at most a quarter block (`len(p) <= blockSize/4`) at offset 0 also takes the ranged path, when the store has prefetch workers (`--prefetch` 1 or more, and a block cache). The ranged path then queues the block for the prefetcher, which downloads the whole block once and caches it, as it already did for reads inside a block. Later reads of that block wait for that download (single flight) or come from the cache.
- **Unchanged.** With `--prefetch 0` or no block cache, a read at offset 0 downloads the whole block as before; otherwise nothing would fill the block and every later read in it would cost one round trip. A read larger than a quarter block and compressed volumes (not seekable) also download the whole block. Encrypted volumes never take the ranged path, at any offset, which also turns off upstream's ranged read inside a block (`boff > 0`). An encrypted volume's `Get` downloads and decrypts the whole object for any range, so every ranged read cost a whole block, and the prefetch it queued downloaded the block a second time. `chunk.Config.Encrypted` controls this. It is set from `format.EncryptKey` in `cmd/mount.go` `getChunkConf` and `cmd/object.go` `getDefaultChunkConf`, which every CLI command uses, and in the app's `internal/mutationbackend`. Ranged reads never write the cache; only a complete, verified block is cached, so no partial block is ever stored.
- **Prefetcher.** Before it downloads, a prefetch now checks the block cache, and checks it again inside the single-flight download. It skips a block that another read has already cached, so a block is not downloaded twice. The prefetch queue still holds 10 blocks and drops a request when full; a dropped block is queued again by the next ranged read in it, and nothing is ever read wrong because of a drop.
- **Gates.** `pkg/chunk/ranged_first_read_test.go` (`TestJM*`): the offset-0 read returns while the whole-block download is held; the prefetcher then fills the block and later reads come from the cache; `--prefetch 0` and large reads keep the whole-block read; a cached block is not prefetched again; on an encrypted volume, a cold read at offset 0 and one inside a block are each one whole-object GET; each of the prefetcher's two cache checks (before queueing, and inside the single-flight download through `fillBlock`) stops a second download on its own; 32 concurrent readers of two cold blocks all read the right bytes with at most one whole-block download per block. CI runs them with `-race`, and the whole package without it (an overlay leaves out upstream's `disk_cache_test.go`, whose `mockey` dependency does not link with this Go).
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm4`. The Manager still requires `-jm3` or later; this patch changes reads only.

`patches/0019-batched-watch-round-trips.patch` cuts the synchronous Redis round trips of a metadata transaction without changing what it watches, reads or writes.
- **Before.** Every WATCH was its own round trip: one when go-redis opened the transaction, one for each `tx.Watch` inside it (the birth/replace guard adds one). Closing the transaction sent UNWATCH, although EXEC had already dropped the watches. Creating a small file and committing its one slice on close took 5 + 7 round trips.
- **Now.** `redisMeta.txn` runs through `watchTxn` (`pkg/meta/redis_watch_batch.go`, JuiceMount-owned). A hook on that one `redis.Tx` holds each WATCH and sends it at the head of the transaction's next read or read pipeline, on the same connection. Redis runs a pipeline in order, so the WATCH is in force before that read, as before. Before MULTI/EXEC or any command that writes (`doSetXattr` sends a bare `HSETNX`), the WATCH is sent alone and its reply awaited, so a refused WATCH never lets a write run. UNWATCH is sent only if a WATCH may still be in force: it is skipped when nothing was sent or the last EXEC committed, was aborted by a watched change, failed with EXECABORT, or was refused by the Redis proxy with JMDENY (the proxy sends DISCARD upstream). `doMknod` reads the parent and its entry in one pipeline. `prepareBirthMutationAttr` (`redis_birth.go`) reads both birth-guard lookup records and the inode's attribute in one pipeline; `doWrite` and `doSetAttr` use that attribute, which their transaction WATCHes from the start. The same create and commit now take 2 + 2 round trips.
- **Failure.** A WATCH that fails fails every later command of that transaction without sending it, so no EXEC runs without its watches, and `txn` returns the WATCH's error as upstream does. Failing means an error reply (such as NOPERM), a connection that broke, or a connection that could not be had at all (a dial or handshake failure). go-redis 9.7.3 sets no error on the commands in the last case, so the hook puts the pipeline's error on them; otherwise the read would return an empty value with no error and the next command would dial a fresh connection with no WATCH. The read pipelines in `doMknod` and `prepareBirthMutationAttr` likewise return any pipeline error that is not a Redis reply, with or without the hook.
- **Callers.** After a `tx.Watch`, every transaction callback issues a command on `tx` before it reads a watched key through another connection (`m.rdb`, as `resolveCase` and `Access` without a full attribute do). That holds for every `txn` callback in `redis.go` and `redis_lock.go`. A new callback must keep it.
- **Scope.** Standalone and Sentinel clients only (`*redis.Client`). Redis Cluster keeps upstream behavior. `JM_REDIS_WATCH_BATCH=0` in the environment of the juicefs process turns the hook off (the two pipelined reads remain).
- **Proxy.** Nothing new reaches the proxy: the same commands, in the same order, on the same connection; only fewer replies are waited for in between. The proxy already reads pipelined commands one by one and records WATCHed keys as it forwards them.
- **Gates.** `pkg/meta/redis_watch_batch_test.go`: round trips per create and commit (counted at the socket), a change after a batched WATCH aborts EXEC, a refused WATCH stops the transaction with nothing written, no WATCH stays on a pooled connection however the callback ends (Redis 7.4 `CLIENT INFO watch=`), a refused WATCH stops a bare write, and a transaction whose first connection cannot be dialled fails instead of committing unwatched. `redis_watch_batch_chaos_test.go` kills random connections of its database, and connections still in their handshake, every 1–8 ms while three sessions create, link, rename, unlink, write, truncate and chmod; afterwards no connection may hold a WATCH and every dentry, inode, link count and parent must agree. `redis_watch_batch_stress_test.go`: two sessions and 16 writers create, write and rename (replacing files) on shared and private folders; every surviving file must have one name, one link and the length its successful writes imply, and the global inode and space counters must match the namespace. Folder statistics drift by the same amount without this patch (upstream credits the parent a racing write saw), so they are reported, not checked. CI runs these with `-race` (the chaos test at 400 operations per worker), with the birth/replace tests and upstream's `TestRedisClient`.
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm5`. The Manager still requires `-jm3` or later.

`patches/0020-demand-read-first.patch` adds `--demand-first`: on a slow link, a read that an application waits for gets its bytes before the prefetcher. The JuiceMount app passes it when the link is slow or metered at mount time; the flag is fixed for the mount's life.
- **Before.** After a ranged first read (patch 0018), the prefetcher downloads the whole block. A second small read in the same block (another NFS read 1 MiB further on) found that download in flight and waited for it (`TryPiggyback`). On a 200 ms link with 1% loss, one 4 MiB block takes 48–55 s, so that read waited about 50 s for 256 KiB.
- **Now.** With the flag (`pkg/chunk/demand_first.go`, JuiceMount-owned), a small ranged read waits for an in-flight whole-block download only when that download should end within about two ranged GETs of that size (0 <= remaining <= 2 x ranged). Whole-block time and ranged time per KiB are smoothed from measurements. A download that has overrun its smoothed time counts as late, not nearly done, so reads do not wait for it. With no measurement yet, the read sends its own GET. Reads that bypass one download may total a quarter block; after that budget, later reads in that block wait for the download, so a sequential reader does not fetch the block twice, unless the download is late: no read ever waits for a late download. The prefetcher of a block waits while ranged demand GETs of other blocks are in flight (a reader that moved on, such as a scrub), for at most 10 s, then checks the block cache again before it downloads. Demand reads of the same block do not hold it: its download is what serves a sequential reader.
- **Cost.** A read that does not wait for the download fetches its bytes twice: at most a quarter block for each download.
- **Unchanged.** Without the flag, everything stays as in patch 0018. Encrypted volumes never take the ranged path, so the flag changes nothing there: one whole-object GET per block.
- **Gates.** `pkg/chunk/demand_first_test.go` (`TestJMDemandFirst*`): the second read in a block returns while the whole-block download is held, and without the flag it waits (control); the prefetcher does not download while a demand read of another block is in flight, is not held by one of its own block, and its wait is bounded; the piggyback rule, including a download past its expected end and the per-download budget; an encrypted volume keeps one whole-object GET.
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm6`. The Manager still requires `-jm3` or later.

`patches/0021-demand-read-spans.patch` adds demand spans to `--demand-first` (`pkg/chunk/demand_spans.go`, JuiceMount-owned) and a lab-only read timeline.
- **Before.** macOS sends FUSE reads of one file one at a time, 128 KiB each. With patch 0020 every 128 KiB miss was its own ranged GET, and each also queued a whole-block prefetch. The lab (laptop, 200 ms RTT, 2026-11-11) measured: with server BBR, a 1 MiB scrub jump cost eight serial GET round trips (about 5.5 s) and fetched about 7 times the bytes it needed; with 1% loss and cubic, where one TCP stream carries about 0.7 Mbit/s, the one prefetch worker downloaded whole 4 MiB blocks one after another (46–60 s each) and demand reads waited behind them.
- **Now.** With the flag, on an unencrypted object store with ranged GETs, a block-cache miss fetches the span around the read: from the 256 KiB part that holds the read, up to 1 MiB, within the block. Each part is its own ranged GET, and the parts run in parallel, so a jump costs about one part's GET and uses several TCP streams. Finished parts stay in memory (at most 128 MiB, 2 minutes; a timer drops expired parts even when no read comes), and the later reads of the span are served from them or wait only for their own part. Only a read that waits for a part counts as a demand read for patch 0020's prefetch defer; the other parts of the span do not. A ranged read queues no whole-block prefetch. When every part of a block has been read, the block goes to the disk cache. Object keys name immutable objects, so a kept part can never be stale.
- **Fallback.** A failed part is dropped (the next read fetches it again), and the read that needed it takes the patch 0020 ranged path.
- **Timeline.** With `JM_READ_TIMELINE=1` in its environment (the app passes it through), the store logs each step of a miss at Info: piggyback waits, ranged, part and whole-block GETs with first byte and end, and prefetch defers. Without it nothing is logged and no log arguments are built.
- **Unchanged.** Without the flag, everything stays as in patch 0020. Encrypted volumes keep one whole-object GET per block.
- **Gates.** `pkg/chunk/demand_spans_test.go` (`TestJMSpan*`, run by CI with `-race`): one GET per part, parts in parallel, no part fetched twice under concurrent reads, reads across parts and at a short block's end, a failed part fetched again, a whole block cached once, the memory bound and expiry, the sweep without reads, demand counted only for awaited parts, and through the store a scrub jump with no whole-block GET. The patch 0020 store tests run with spans off.
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm7`.

`patches/0022-reserved-inode-mkdir.patch` lets the JuiceMount app answer an NFS MKDIR before the folder exists on the volume, without the folder's file id changing later. macOS treats a changed file id on a folder it holds as a stale handle.
- **Messages.** Two control-file messages (`.control`, as `juicefs rmr` and `info` use): `JMReserveInodes` (1101) takes up to 4096 numbers from the volume's inode counter (`nextInode`, the counter every client allocates from), so no client will allocate them. `JMMkdirInode` (1102) creates one directory with one of those numbers. `JMReleaseInodes` (1103) gives back numbers that were not used, so restarts of the app do not fill the cap; it returns how many were still held (0 after a juicefs restart). Replies: errno, then the first number and the count (reserve); errno (mkdir); errno and the released count (release).
- **Same checks.** `baseMeta.Mknod` now calls `mknod` with an optional pre-assigned inode; with 0 it allocates as upstream. `JMMkdirInode` goes through that path: name checks, trash and read-only refusals, quota, the parent's write permission for the caller's uid and gid, and the same engine transaction as `Mkdir`, so the RESP proxy's project leases see the same commands.
- **One use, this process only.** Reserved numbers live in memory (`pkg/meta/jm_reserved_inode.go`, JuiceMount-owned) and end with the process; at most 65,536 are held. A number is removed when used. After a refusal that wrote nothing (EEXIST, ENOENT, EROFS, EACCES and the like) it stays reserved; after any other error it is never offered again, because an ambiguous EXEC reply may have committed it. An unknown number is refused with ESRCH and nothing is written; the app then creates the folder with an ordinary mkdir.
- **Kernel cache.** After a create, the kernel entry for the name is invalidated, as `rmr` does.
- **Gates.** `pkg/meta/jm_reserved_inode_test.go` (memkv): the folder gets the reserved number; an ordinary create never takes a reserved number; a used or forged number is refused with nothing written; a refusal keeps the number; reservations do not overlap; a release gives back only unused numbers, once.
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm8`. The Manager still requires `-jm3` or later.

`patches/0023-batched-rename-reads.patch` cuts a Redis rename from 5 to 3 round trips. The app's drainer publishes every saved file with a no-replace rename of its private stage in the same folder, and JuiceFS runs one transaction per folder at a time (`txLock` on the parent), so these round trips set how fast saved files reach the server on a distant link.
- **Before.** After the source entry: the replacement guard record (`replaceguard`), then the destination entry, then the attributes of both parents and the source, each its own round trip.
- **Now.** The source attribute and the guard record are WATCHed, then the guard, the destination entry and the three attributes are read in one pipeline. Every read key is WATCHed before its read: both parents and the destination folder's entries since the transaction began. Replacing an existing file WATCHes the victim and reads its attribute afterwards: one more round trip (4 in total).
- **Unchanged.** The commands, keys and checks are the same; only the order of the reads and the number of waits change. Protected (enrolled) renames still WATCH their required keys before `checkProtectedRename` reads them.
- **Gates.** `pkg/meta/redis_rename_batch_test.go` counts round trips at the socket (3 for a new name, 4 for a replace), checks the result and that no WATCH stays on the connection. The patch 0019 chaos and stress tests (concurrent create, link, rename, unlink, write with connection kills) pass unchanged.

`patches/0024-small-upload-lane.patch` adds `--small-uploads N` (default 0, off): upload slots that only small saves may use, so the fsync or close of a small file does not wait behind a large file's blocks.
- **Before.** Every block PUT took one of the `--max-uploads` slots, and waiting PUTs took them in arrival order. The app mounts with `--max-uploads 4` (cellular resilience: four 4 MiB flows at most) and without writeback, so an fsync returns only after its PUTs. On a thin far link a large render's drain keeps all four slots busy with 4 MiB blocks. In the laptop lab (200 ms, 1% loss, server BBR) each small save's fsync took about 38 s, and small saves reached the server in batches of four every 40 s.
- **Now.** `pkg/chunk/jm_upload_lane.go` (JuiceMount-owned) adds a second pool of N slots. `fileWriter.flush` (fsync and close) marks each slice it flushes when the whole file is at most 1 MiB (`pkg/vfs/jm_upload_lane.go`, `SetSmallSave`); a slice already frozen by a background flush is marked too, if it is not done. A marked slice of at most 1 MiB takes a free lane slot first, otherwise the first slot of either pool that frees. Every other block uses the `--max-uploads` slots only, in arrival order as before.
- **Background flushes never qualify.** JuiceFS also finishes a slice from timers: one older than 5 s or idle for 1 s (`flushAll`), one older than 10 s (`commitThread`), and a full chunk. A large file written slower than about 1.6 Mbit/s (a drain throttled to a thin uplink) is uploaded in such slices of under 1 MiB each. They are not marked, so the large file keeps to `--max-uploads` PUTs. The fsync of a file larger than 1 MiB is not marked either, even when the slice it flushes is small.
- **Bounds.** At most `--max-uploads` + N PUTs run at once; large blocks never hold more than `--max-uploads`. The lane adds at most N MiB in flight. With N = 0 nothing changes (upstream behaviour). `object_request_uploading` counts both pools.
- **Unchanged.** Durability and order: a block's result still reaches the slice only after its PUT, and `Finish` (so fsync and close) still waits for every block. Retries, timeouts, compression and encryption run as before inside the PUT. Writeback staging and delayed uploads keep the shared slots only.
- **App.** `health/fuse.go` passes `--small-uploads 2`, or 1 on the metered read policy (a thin uplink with a 5 min PUT deadline, where each extra PUT slows the four large ones). `JM_JFS_SMALL_UPLOADS` (0 to 4) overrides; 0 is the field rollback, and any other value turns the slots off with a warning.
- **Gates.** `pkg/chunk/jm_upload_lane_test.go` (`TestJMUploadLane*`, run by CI with `-race`): a marked small save's Finish returns while four large PUTs are held, and without the lane it waits (control); unmarked small slices (background flushes) stay in the shared slots; Finish waits for the PUT and returns its error; under mixed load large PUTs never exceed `--max-uploads`, all PUTs never exceed the sum, every slice reads back and no slot leaks; only marked slices of at most 1 MiB qualify; a small block prefers a lane slot; an encrypted, lz4-compressed volume behaves the same and reads back. `pkg/vfs/jm_upload_lane_test.go` (CI, `-race`) runs the real paths: a slowly written file flushed by the idle timer never takes the lane, the fsync of a small file takes it while the shared slot is held, and the fsync of a file over 1 MiB does not, even for a small slice.
- **Version.** The build suffix moved to `-jm9`. The Manager still requires `-jm3` or later.
